Vanessa — quick draft language below that Legal prefers. I kept it narrow to reduce downstream obligations while addressing FinTechCo's core needs. Feel free to paste directly into the docx and send to Priya.

1) Breach notification (proposed):
"Vendor will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer with an initial notification of a confirmed or reasonably suspected security incident affecting Customer data within seventy-two (72) hours of Vendor's discovery. Such initial notification will include a description of the nature of the incident, the categories of data and affected systems, and any immediate mitigation steps taken. Vendor will provide subsequent updates as information becomes available and will cooperate with Customer's incident response team. In the event Vendor determines there is active exploitation or ongoing exfiltration that materially increases risk to Customer, Vendor will escalate and provide continuous updates until containment is achieved."

Rationale: 72 hours balances forensic review time with the customer's need for timely notice. We accept the requirement to cooperate; we push back on a hard 24-hour window because it can incentivize incomplete, inaccurate reporting.

2) Subprocessors (proposed):
"Vendor will provide Customer with written notice of any new subprocessor at least thirty (30) days prior to engaging such subprocessor. For subprocessors that will process personal data or otherwise pose a material security or regulatory risk to Customer, Customer may object in writing within fourteen (14) days of receipt of notice; the parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve any objection. If the parties cannot reach agreement within thirty (30) days, Vendor will use reasonable efforts to provide a functionally equivalent alternative or, where feasible, cease using the subprocessor for Customer's processing."

Note: we should be explicit that notices are via email to the security/compliance contact and include a link to the subprocessor inventory (we can host a minimal page or provide a CSV). Also propose using SCCs for EU transfers and mapping to our KMS/HSM controls in the data transfer annex.

DocuSign/Execution logistics: if FinTechCo prefers DocuSign we can send from our corporate envelope. I'll prepare the envelope after Vanessa confirms the redline. If FinTechCo requires AdobeSign only, we can route through their platform but will need procurement to confirm signatory details.

I'll also prepare a short incident playbook blurb we can attach that describes contact points and expected timelines (useful to close on the cooperation ask).

Priya — thanks for sending the redline and for the quick turnaround from your team. We reviewed and discussed internally and would like to propose a compromise intended to meet FinTechCo's risk needs while keeping operational accuracy:

- Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial notification within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery that contains a preliminary summary (nature of incident, affected systems, initial mitigation). We commit to a targeted 24-hour acknowledgement to confirm receipt and that an investigation is underway. Where there is active exploitation or material exfiltration, we will escalate and provide more frequent updates (we've proposed contract language to that effect).
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide 30 days' written notice for new subprocessors. For subprocessors that process personal data or present material risk, FinTechCo may object in writing within 14 days; we'll use commercially reasonable efforts to resolve and, where necessary, provide alternatives or transition assistance. We will also give FinTechCo access to a maintained subprocessor inventory (CSV or hosted page) in advance of engagement.
- Data transfers: Redwood will use EU/UK SCCs and provide the Data Transfer Addendum referenced in the DPA.

I've attached our proposed redline reflecting the language above (redwood_proposed_dpa_redlines_20261128.docx). If this aligns, we can finalize and send via DocuSign — I'll create the envelope and share the link (DocuSign is the faster path for us).
